title: How is a change-of-destination fee charged on a Container Bookings booking?
content:
## When this applies
This entry covers the Container Bookings product line. A change of port of discharge accepted on a booking owes one change-of-destination fee, and the fee is owed from the day the change was logged, whether or not it was charged at that time. A change that was logged without its fee is charged when the booking is next handled, as long as the booking still accepts amendment charges under the amendment rules.

## Business effect of the charge
Charging the fee adds one change-of-destination fee entry, dated today, to the booking's charge history and raises the booking's outstanding charges by exactly the amount booked. The booking's port of discharge, sailing, containers and status are not touched.

## How it is invoked
The charge is made with **charge_destination_change_fee_9814adc0**, an internal tool that must first be unlocked (unlock) and then called (call) by the agent. The tool books exactly the amount passed in; it does not compute an amount and does not check any business condition.

## Parameters
| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| booking_id | the booking reference number of the booking being charged, as returned by the booking lookup for the verified customer | identifier |
| vessel_voyage | the vessel and voyage shown on the change-of-destination amendment entry this fee charges, taken from the booking's charge history | verbatim: copied character for character, preserving every letter, digit, space and punctuation mark, with no translation, normalisation, addition or deletion |
| fee_usd | the change-of-destination fee to book, in USD | a positive decimal amount with 2 decimal places; a value given with more digits is rounded half-to-even to 2 decimal places when booked |

## Return
The tool returns a text rendering of a dictionary describing the booked entry: booking_event_id (reference of the new fee entry in the charge history), booking_id (the booking charged), charge_code (always pod_change_fee), vessel_voyage (the sailing recorded on the entry), amount_usd (the fee booked, USD with 2 decimal places), event_date (YYYY-MM-DD, the booking date of the entry) and charges_due_usd (the booking's outstanding charges after the fee, USD with 2 decimal places). A returned booking_event_id means the fee is on the account. The new entry is recorded with the amendment kind pod_change, also carries the booking's equipment type, and records no container count, because the amount passed in is already the whole amount of the entry.

## Points of judgement
**Does the call change the destination itself?** No. It only books the fee for a change already on the booking.

**Is a change logged last week, but never charged, still chargeable today?** Yes, when the booking still accepts amendment charges; the fee has been owed since the day the change was logged.
